design.alternative_shell: 1 <= D_KL(Q||P) <= 1.1, Q Gaussian N(mu,r), mu>=0; negative mu by sign symmetry

simulator.early_neighbor_groups: U=P^b; A=P^(T-b); V=P^x Q^(g-x) because b=g=16; B=Q^(H-b)
simulator.late_neighbor_groups: U=P^b; A=P^(T-b) P^x Q^(g-x); V=Q^b; B=Q^(H-b)
simulator.shared_path_atoms: U, Apre, P^x, Q^(g-x), Q^16, Q^16, Q^16 generated once per path from exact Gaussian subgroup mean plus chi-square within-SSE and reused by both candidates
simulator.snml_regret_increment: d_n=(n+1)/2 log n - n/2 log(n-1) - 1/2 log(2e) + log Gamma((n-1)/2)-log Gamma(n/2); r_b(N)=sum_{n=b+1}^N d_n
simulator.seed_rule: anchor integer j uses seed=20000000+j*1000+x for offset x; j ranges are explicit in anchors

transport.anchor_radius: rho_a=min_x kl(0.09 || U_CP(a,x))/(64-x), where U_CP is the direct JOINT neighboring-pair failure upper bound
transport.path_kl: For any target Q and anchor Qa under offset x, D(path_Q||path_Qa)=(64-x) D_KL(Q||Qa).
transport.binary_data_processing: If D_KL(Q||Qa)<=rho_a then joint-pair failure at Q is <=0.09 for every offset x.

anchor_construction.same_level_adaptation: At each fixed KL level start from lower variance endpoint, r=1 and upper variance endpoint; compute the all-offset KL transport interval and repeatedly insert the geometric midpoint of the largest uncovered log-r gap until that exact level is covered.

continuum_shell_cover.outside_cell_test: For each rectangle, exact min/max of I over the rectangle are bounded using convex g(r)=r-1-log r; discard if Imax<1 or Imin>1.1.
continuum_shell_cover.cell_ball_test: D_KL(target||anchor) is jointly convex/separable in (mu,r); its maximum on a rectangle is attained at a corner. A cell is certified if one anchor's minimum all-offset rho exceeds the maximum of the four corner KL values.
continuum_shell_cover.split_rule: Bisect the larger normalized span; mu arithmetically, r geometrically. Start from the full bounding rectangle.
continuum_shell_cover.result: No uncovered shell cells. Therefore, conditional on the Clopper-Pearson anchor bounds and ordinary floating-point arithmetic used for cell/anchor calculations, every Gaussian Q in the full 2D shell 1<=KL(Q||P)<=1.1 has neighboring-pair failure probability <=0.09 for all 17 discrete offsets.

engineering_counterexample_search.coarse_scan: 6 KL radii from 1 to 1.1 x 31 log-r points x all 17 offsets, 500 shared-path draws/point.
engineering_counterexample_search.interpretation: No mixed mean/variance point in this scan exceeded the exact-level I=1 region; empirical failure generally decreased outward. This is engineering evidence only, not the continuum proof.

scope_limits: This covers only the Gaussian shell 1<=KL<=1.1, not every KL>=1.
Coverage arithmetic is ordinary float64 with no directed-rounding/interval audit yet.
The randomized guarantee is over offline Monte Carlo certification randomness; it is not an analytic finite-sample power theorem.
No claim is made for non-Gaussian or heavy-tailed alternatives.
exact_next_action: Extend the same direct-joint anchor-ball plus convex (mu,r)-rectangle cover outward from KL 1.1, first to 1.25 and then adaptively until a high-information analytic lower-tail handoff can replace finite shells. In parallel replay the r76 cell and anchor inequalities with directed-rounding/interval arithmetic. If outer-shell anchor count stops decreasing or a mixed-direction failure spike appears, retain a finite certified shell and derive a separate high-information concentration bound rather than assuming radial monotonicity.
